extracted.intended_audience: poets, American writers, and readers interested in defining/evaluating American poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for poems and volumes intended to express the spirit and future of American democracy — emphasising nativity, scientific/kosmic scope, emotional directness, and social function. Applies to poets assessing their work's alignment with a democratic, national, and modern poetic project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual thematic veins: politics and the thought of immortality
rubrics_metrics.description: Embody in a volume two distinct veins or strata — politics on one hand, and the pensive thought of immortality on the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author states: "I have not hesitated to embody in, and run through the volume, two altogether distinct veins, or strata--politics for one, and for the other, the pensive thought of immortality." The present book therefore divides into these two veins after its minor episodes, and uses both prose and poetic forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry should radiate democracy's growth in literary, artistic, and religious expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The true growth-characteristics of the New World democracy should radiate more in superior literary, artistic and religious expressions than merely in republican forms or frequent elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: "That the true growth-characteristics of the democracy of the New World are henceforth to radiate in superior literary, artistic and religious expressions, far more than in its republican forms..." Evaluate works by how well they embody and project the democratic spirit culturally and spiritually, not merely politically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political mission: fuse state prerogatives with central national oneness
rubrics_metrics.description: Political content should recognise and aim at the practical solution of combining individual state prerogatives with the indispensable necessity of centrality and Oneness (national identity, sovereign Union).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prose asserts a vital political mission of the United States which the literature may reflect: "the fusion, thorough compatibility and junction of individual State prerogatives, with the indispensable necessity of centrality and Oneness--the national identity power." Works with political themes should show awareness of this national-unifying aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build from foundational works but evolve into new stems
rubrics_metrics.description: Later works should grow out of and be grounded in prior foundational volumes (e.g., Leaves of Grass), using them as "deep soil" while producing more definite roots and stems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The chants of 'Leaves of Grass' ... serve as the indispensable deep soil, or basis, out of which ... could come the roots and stems more definitely indicated by these later pages." Guidance: acknowledge lineage while extending themes and forms rather than merely repeating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocalize the kosmic spirit: integrate scientism and vastness
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern poems must vocalize the vastness, splendor and reality which scientism has invested man and the universe with — the 'kosmic spirit' should be the background of first-class songs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance: "the real poems of the present, ever solidifying and expanding into the future, must vocalize the vastness and splendor and reality with which scientism has invested man and the universe..." Evaluate whether poetry incorporates modern scientific vision and a sense of cosmic scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept modern science while recognizing the eternal soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry should joyfully accept modern science but also recognize a higher flight: the eternal soul and spiritual/religious dimensions must remain present and be amplified, not negated, by scientism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Only... there remains ever recognized still a higher flight, a higher fact, the eternal soul of man... which it is to be the greatest office of scientism... to free from fables... and launch forth in renew'd faith." Good poetry integrates science and spirituality, using science to free and enlarge religious imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's religious role: free theology from fables and enrich it
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry (and scientism via poetry) should help free religious thought from crude fables and superstitions and enable a more splendid theology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author links scientism to the opportunity for "a more splendid theology, and for ampler and diviner songs." Evaluate poems by their capacity to renew religious ideas in enlarged, less superstitious forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style for the soul: fluid, aerial, and intentionally obscure
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing the soul, poetic style should be less definite in form and outline, becoming vista, music, half-tints, and may deliberately leave dim escapes and outlets rather than hyper-clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: "Poetic style, when address'd to the soul, is less definite form, outline, sculpture, and becomes vista, music, half-tints... must leave dim escapes and outlets... obscure to those of little or no imagination." This justifies measured obscurity and atmospheric, suggestive technique as a feature, not a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry should leave room for imagination; avoid over-definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Good poetry often initiates, suggests and leaves openings for imagination instead of fully defining or finishing every idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author defends charges of obscurity: "human thought, poetry or melody, must leave dim escapes and outlets... indispensable to the highest purposes." Evaluate works by their capacity to open rather than close meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / autochthonic nativity: no imitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A nation's poetry must be autochthonic and original; imitations of foreign models are inadequate — 'no imitations will do.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: "The stamp of entire and finished greatness... must be sternly withheld till it has put what it stands for in the blossom of original, first-class poems. No imitations will do." Judge poetry by its indigenous voice and capacity to reflect native life and identity rather than faithfully mimic the English tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce national types and physiognomy in verse
rubrics_metrics.description: First-class poems are twined with the nation's types of personal character and individuality; poetry should produce native physiognomy — unique shapes, forms, and manners of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "With the poems of a first-class land are twined... its types of personal character, of individuality... its own physiognomy..." Evaluate whether poetry creates and justifies distinct national characters and manners in its art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sing the 'Poem of average Identity' — value ordinary lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Poems should celebrate 'average Identity' — the ordinary farmer, seafarer, mechanic, laborer — presenting everyday life as central and worthy of poetic treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author describes Leaves of Grass as intended "to be the Poem of average Identity..." and argues that to the highest democratic view, a man is most acceptable in living well his practical lot. Evaluate whether poetry dignifies ordinary life and civic roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as radical utterance from Emotions and Physique, not scholastic exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet should produce 'radical utterance out of the Emotions and the Physique' rather than an intellectual or scholastic effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "It is imperatively and ever to be borne in mind that 'Leaves of Grass' entire is not to be construed as an intellectual or scholastic effort... but more as a radical utterance out of the Emotions and the Physique." Consider emotional directness, physical immediacy, and visceral force as merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster comradeship and democratic social bonding
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry (e.g., the 'Calamus' cluster) should cultivate comradeship and sane affection of man for man as a means to weld and anneal the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "In my opinion, it is by a fervent, accepted development of comradeship... that the United States of the future... are to be most effectually welded together." Evaluate political/social poems by their capacity to promote civic unity and interpersonal solidarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of future poetry: to arouse and initiate, not to define or finish
rubrics_metrics.description: The poetry of the future aims at the free expression of emotion and principally to arouse and initiate responses in readers rather than to provide finished definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: "The poetry of the future aims at the free expression of emotion... and to arouse and initiate, more than to define or finish." Prioritise evocative, experimental, and initiatory work over neatly closed, doctrinal poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid being over-sophisticated, courtly, or purely ornamental
rubrics_metrics.description: Antipattern: poems that are overly labored, perfumed, or 'inside elegance'—showing a 'scholar and conventional gentleman' rather than naive, democratic freedom—are less suited to the American poetic mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of Tennyson: "Never one democratic page; nay, not a line, not a word; never free and naïve poetry, but involved, labored, quite sophisticated..." Use this as a warning against excessive refinement that distances poetry from democratic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate useful foreign influences but transform them to native scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept and work over foreign (European/feudal) poetic nutriment where beneficial, but transform and popularize it for Western tenancy rather than uncritically importing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "If we are not to hospitably receive and complete the inaugurations of the old civilizations... what on earth are we for?" Guidance: be open to useful traditions but adapt them to produce autochthonic results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raciness and capacity for reproduction (authenticity and sustainability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid exoticism and a 'fatal want of raciness' which makes verse unsustainably derivative; national poetry should have a principle of reproduction and internal evidence of locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted criticism from the London Times: "American verse... is afflicted... with a fatal want of raciness... an exotic... with an exuberance of gorgeous blossom, but no principle of reproduction." Evaluate works for internal evidence of native place, voice, and the ability to seed further native work.
